Modules shown here come from third-party stores and **have NOT been security-reviewed**.

The source KernelSU ships with is this official registry (modules.kernelsu.org), and this app uses it by default. The registry reviews each module's first submission against its rules — but there is **no code audit and no malware scanning**: the review checks for spam, abuse, ID squatting and the like, not what a module does on your device. Later updates are **published automatically without review**, and neither signatures nor developer identities are verified. The candidate stores you can add with one tap are **not reviewed by us at all**.

Modules run with root privileges and can read and write system partitions, your app data and network traffic. A malicious module — or one from a compromised author account — can **make the device fail to boot (a hard brick), destroy data, steal accounts or money, or leak private information**, often with no easy recovery.

We offer custom stores and the built-in candidates only to make finding modules easier. That is not a recommendation, endorsement or guarantee of anything in them. Judge for yourself, and **accept the risk**: only install modules from sources you trust.

The Coolapk community index is a different case: its modules are uploaded by Coolapk users on their own, to make the modules scattered across Coolapk posts easier to find. **Nothing in it has been reviewed by a human for safety** — turning that source on means **you take the consequences yourself**.

Why only the original package can be uploaded

The zip stored in the index is what other people install. During installation the installer shipped inside the module (customize.sh / install.sh / the installer under META-INF) picks the matching ABI variant, sets file permissions and checks the system version. Skip any of that and the module installs wrong.

An installed module has no installer left in its directory: it is deleted the moment installation finishes, and META-INF is never extracted. A zip rebuilt from that directory reaches other people without an installer, so installation silently falls back to plain extraction and none of those steps happen.

Uploads therefore only accept the zip the author published. If the original zip was kept at install time, the entry on this page opens it directly.

The zip has no installer at all (neither customize.sh, install.sh nor the META-INF installer). That usually means it was rebuilt from an installed module: the installer is deleted as soon as installation completes, so the module directory can never still contain it.

Installing such a zip, the manager finds no script and silently extracts everything with defaults — picking the right ABI, setting permissions and the environment checks never happen.

Upload the zip the author published instead. If the original was kept at install time, the entry on this page opens it directly.

Temporarily put this string into your Coolapk signature
Open Coolapk (Me > Edit profile > Signature), paste this string there and save. This step proves the UID really is yours; once verified you can switch back to your own signature at any time.

Uploads are public, and every module you upload runs with root privileges on the devices of everyone who installs it. That is why we need to know who uploaded each one: your Coolapk UID is recorded so a module can always be traced back to its uploader, and we require a Coolapk account of level Lv2 or above to deter casual abuse (the signature check only proves that the UID you entered is really yours).
Coolapk level Lv2 or above required.
